#!/usr/bin/env bash
# 08-power-management.sh -- Section 8: Power management (TLP)
#
# Overrides are written to a dedicated drop-in file under /etc/tlp.d/,
# never to /etc/tlp.conf itself. TLP's own precedence order is:
#   intrinsic defaults -> /etc/tlp.d/*.conf -> /etc/tlp.conf (read last, wins)
# so if the user has ever set any of these keys in /etc/tlp.conf -- by hand,
# or it came pre-set some other way -- that user value wins automatically
# and this script never has to detect, guess at, or touch it.
#
# TLP >= 1.10 semantics (verified against TLP 1.10.1 on Fedora 44): the
# _AC/_BAT/_SAV suffixes select the "performance"/"balanced"/"power-saver"
# TLP profile -- the same three states GNOME's Power Mode toggle and tlp-pd
# expose via D-Bus -- NOT the AC/battery power source as in older TLP
# versions. _SAV falls back to _BAT for any key left unset. We target _BAT
# (balanced) since that's meant to be the safe default profile, and pin
# TLP_PROFILE_AC=BAL so plugging in the charger doesn't auto-switch to the
# performance profile (TLP's own default is TLP_PROFILE_AC=PRF, i.e. jump to
# performance on AC). Leaving _AC (performance profile) untouched means
# explicitly selecting "Performance" in the GNOME toggle still gets real
# turbo boost, as that choice should mean.
compressed: #@ ext TLP>=1.10 _AC/_BAT/_SAV=mode; /etc/tlp.conf wins; _SAV->_BAT; set _BAT=BAL, AC=BAL; leave _AC for GNOME Performance
